prompt: On a reviewer-owned disposable Ceph deployment or faithful isolated harness with synthetic data, diagnose, contain, recover and remove an unfamiliar client-I/O incident. The reviewer secretly injects one identity/map defect, one pool/PG/CRUSH durability defect, one OSD/network/capacity defect, one RBD/OpenStack writer or upgrade defect and one observability/integrity/cleanup defect. Work without model-answer material and stay inside the approved boundary.
deliverables: Named user I/O, data invariant, SLO, consistency/durability, RPO/RTO and refusal conditions
Exact release/deployment/client/OpenStack/hardware topology and physical failure-domain map
Safe identity record for FSID, config source, cephx entity/capabilities and map epochs
Object path joining application request, pool/image/object, PG, up/acting sets, primary, OSDs and devices
Pool protection and CRUSH analysis including size/min_size or K+M, rules and simulated failures
PG state/acting-history, peering, availability, cleanliness, scrub and integrity timeline
OSD up/down and in/out, device/BlueStore, public/cluster network and operation-queue evidence
Raw, eligible, amplified, per-pool MAX AVAIL, fullness and failure/movement-reserve calculation
Recovery/backfill progress and foreground-user SLI comparison with stop gates
RBD/OpenStack resource, snapshot/clone, lock/watcher, client and single-writer evidence
Least-privilege identity, key protection, tenant and data-security review
Release-compatible change/upgrade sequence, canary, pause, rollback and recovery boundary
Containment that rejects destructive repair, lost-object action and unfenced writer movement
Representative client/application I/O and data-correctness validation
Supported reconciliation and exact cleanup proof for every temporary identity, mapping and object
Blameless review with owners, acceptance tests, retest, residual risk and bounded claims
evidenceRequirements: All work remains on reviewer-owned disposable local infrastructure or a faithful harness with synthetic data
No production cluster, public target, external cloud, real keyring, customer data or uncontrolled I/O is used
The reviewer owns hidden defects, expected boundaries, stop authority, scoring and cleanup confirmation
FSID, release, configuration source, client identity and map epoch are bound before diagnosis
No secret key or sensitive object content appears in submitted evidence
Monitor quorum, manager view, OSD state, PG state and client outcome remain separate claims
Pool protection and CRUSH failure domains are verified against physical topology
Object-to-PG-to-acting-set evidence is preserved before mutation
Raw free capacity never substitutes for eligible MAX AVAIL, fullness and failure reserve
Recovery progress and foreground user impact are measured together
Inconsistent or unfound objects cause refusal until authority and consequences are reviewed
RBD writer movement or lock handling requires old-writer fencing
Mixed versions and minimum client/OSD compatibility are explicit
Unexpected data, identity, host or tenant impact converts the exercise to incident handling
Every claim is bounded to the exact versions, topology, policy, workload and observation window
Every finding has an owner, measurable acceptance evidence and retest or explicit risk acceptance

rubric.observableEvidence: Binds user/data contract, FSID, release, cephx, client and map epochs
Explains pool, object, PG, CRUSH, acting sets and replica/shard policy
Proves daemon membership, device/BlueStore, network, queues and acknowledgement
Calculates eligible capacity/fullness/reserve and controls recovery contention
Uses acting history, scrub and safe repair/recovery decisions
Correlates resources, locks/watchers, clients, fencing and one writer
Uses least privilege, protected keys, isolation, data controls and audit
Uses compatible sequence, canary, pause, rollback and recovery proof
Proves representative I/O, invariants, reconciliation and artifact absence
Produces bounded claims, residual risk, owned actions and retest evidence
